cards.back: Finding the stored items whose embeddings point in nearly the same direction as the query's embedding. It matches on meaning, not shared words.

cards.front: Why embed the query with the exact index model and version?
cards.back: Vectors from two different models live in unrelated spaces, so comparing them gives meaningless scores rather than an error.
Compare the query with every stored vector and keep the k best. Cost per query is N vectors × d dimensions multiply-adds.

cards.front: When is exact search the right answer?
cards.back: Small corpora up to roughly 100k to 1M vectors, very selective filters that leave few rows, and as ground truth for measuring an ANN index.
A greedy descent through the upper layers of the graph, then a beam search on layer 0 that keeps the ef best candidates open.
The HNSW beam width at query time (default 40 in pgvector). Raising it improves recall and slows queries; it must be at least k.
How much the ANN index approximates away, measured against exact k-NN over the same vectors. Typically 0.95 to 0.99; fix it with ef_search or nprobe.
Whether search finds the chunks that answer the question, measured against a labelled golden set. Fix it upstream: chunks, model, hybrid search, filters.
Search a compressed form (int8, binary, PQ), shortlist k × 4 to 10, then re-score the shortlist with full vectors and keep k.
50 to 100 candidates from vector search, a reranker to order them, and 5 to 10 chunks into the prompt.
Picks results one at a time, rewarding similarity to the query and penalising similarity to what is already picked. λ around 0.5 to 0.8 usually works.

quiz.q: In pgvector you ask for 100 results with the default ef_search of 40. What do you get?
choices: An error saying ef is too small
quiz.why: A query returns at most hnsw.ef_search rows unless iterative scans are enabled.

quiz.q: Index recall is 0.99 but retrieval recall is 0.6. What should you do?
choices: Add more HNSW links per node
Fix chunks, the model, hybrid search or filters
quiz.why: The index faithfully returns the nearest vectors; they are just the wrong passages, so the problem is upstream.

quiz.q: With unnormalised vectors and dot product, what goes wrong?
choices: Long vectors win even when they point the wrong way
quiz.why: Dot product depends on length as well as angle, which is why unnormalised vectors are risky.

quiz.q: Why is a fixed similarity threshold like 0.8 fragile?
choices: Each model spreads scores differently, and 0.8 means different things per query
quiz.why: Similarity scores are not probabilities; calibrate any threshold on labelled data.

quiz.q: FY2023 and FY2024 reports keep getting confused. What is the fix?
choices: Metadata filters extracted from the query
quiz.why: Numbers and years embed almost identically; a filter does the exact work.

quiz.q: Going from 0.95 to 0.995 index recall in the illustrative sweep costs about how much latency?
quiz.why: The curve flattens: ef_search 40 to 200 goes from 2.3 ms to 8.9 ms.

quiz.q: Why does re-scoring recover most of the accuracy lost to compression?
choices: The compressed form only needs to get the right items onto the shortlist
quiz.why: The full vectors then order the shortlist precisely.
